# See tools/claimcheck.py for why this exists. In two days three repos in this
# toolchain were found publishing a score no gate had ever printed -- the docs
# site's "498/498 byte-exact modules" for aowlsem (an hconv-site census reworded
# into a module count; the real figure was 46/55), aowlc's "73/73" for a script
# printing 66/67, and its "77/77" for one printing 78/78.
# This repo's exposure is the "Verified" section. `fib(20)=6765`,
# `ack(3,4)=125`, `fib(25)=75025` are stated as a property of the pipeline, and
# no gate here prints them. tests/raises.sh does now compile and RUN a produced
# binary -- so the old wording, "NEITHER gate here runs a produced binary", is
# no longer true and has been corrected -- but it runs ONE regression case and
# checks ITS output; it computes no fib and no ack. differential.sh and game.sh
# still stop at byte-comparing the lowered .c.aif. There is still no script in
# this tree that would print those three numbers. That is the 498/498 shape exactly -- a true-
# sounding number whose producer does not exist -- so it is filed UNATTRIBUTED
# and fails the run until somebody either writes the script or restates the
# claim as aifmony's, naming aifmony's command.

Either add a script that does it and paste what it printed, or state the claim as 'aifmony's driver reports' with the aifmony command that reports it.
